newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-Portugal Telecom makes Telefonica connection.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Portugal Telecom makes Telefonica connection.

text.p: Portugal Telecom announced on Tuesday an accord involving a share exchange with Spain's Telefonica, its larger Iberian neighbour, forging a new link in its emerging international network.

The news came only one day after the Portuguese declared they had opted for the Anglo-American venture Concert as their global partners in the increasingly alliance-denominated telecommunications scene.
A company spokeswoman gave no details of the latest accord, saying that all would be revealed after the deal had been signed on Wednesday. But she confirmed that stakes would be swapped.
"PT confirms an accord with Telefonica with a share exchange," she told Reuters.

She would not say whether the Spanish company's stake in Telecom would be between 3.0 and 3.5 percent, with Telecom in turn taking one percent in Telefonica, as reported by Spanish newspapers on Tuesday.
But the scope of the deal ranged well beyond a share swap, she said.

Although no further official information was immediately available, analysts said that the deal would probably involve cooperation in exploiting the rapidly developing market in Latin American where both companies have historical links.
"I suspect the focus is going to be Latin America," said James Golob, telecommunications analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
Portugal Telecom, in which the state is preparing to sell a further stake to go below a 50 percent holding, already has an international alliance with Telebras, the main Brazilian operator.
Telefonica also has operations in Brazil as well as in Chile, Argentina, Venezuela and Peru.
"It makes sense. Both companies are targetting Latin America," echoed Jose Antonio Goncalves of Lisbon brokers Tottadealer.
Portugal Telecom's share price rose over two percent to 6,276 escudos on the news which was seen as strengthing the company's international position.
But the alliance also raised a fresh question mark over the future place of Telefonica in the rapidly evolving system of international liaisons between the world's top telecommunications groups.

In announcing the tie-up with Concert, the alliance of British Telecom and the U.S. MCI, the companies said that exploiting the potential of the Latin American market would be one of the main purposes of the cooperation.
Telefonica, however, belongs to the rival Unisource international grouping which is led by U.S. giant AT&T.

Analysts said that it made little sense for Portugal Telecom to have agreed a link with Concert, with its Latin American ambitions, only to agree a potentially conflicting deal with another operator 24 hours later.
There have been repeated rumours that Telefonica is about to jump ship and Portugal Telecom's announcement of the Concert deal initially referred to such announcement as being pending.
This was later denied by Telefonica.
"It sounds as if it is all related. There must have been some last minute glitch which is why nothing has been announced yet," said Golob.
